title: Daily Practice: Ch 11 Electricity
subject: Science
instructions: One day at a time, about 25 minutes each: Day 1 on the day you study the chapter, then Day 2 and Day 3. Write answers in your notebook and check them with the key the same day. Copy every mistake into your error log.
Formulas: Q = It · V = W/Q · V = IR · R = ρL/A · series R = R_{1} + R_{2} + … · parallel 1/R = 1/R_{1} + 1/R_{2} + … · P = VI = I^{2}R = V^{2}/R · H = I^{2}Rt · 1 kWh = 3.6 × 10^{6} J

sections.title: Day 1: Current, potential difference and Ohm's law

questions.q: One ampere is equal to:
questions.answer: (a) 1 coulomb per second (1 J/s is a watt; 1 J/C is a volt)

questions.q: At a constant temperature, the resistance of a wire does NOT depend on:
options: the potential difference applied across it
the material it is made of
questions.answer: (b) the potential difference applied across it: if V is doubled, I doubles and R stays the same

questions.q: A current of 2 A flows through a wire for 3 minutes. The charge that flows is:
The potential difference between two points is the:
options: work done to move a unit charge from one point to the other
questions.answer: (b) work done per unit charge: V = W/Q

questions.q: Draw the circuit symbols for: a cell, a battery, a closed plug key, a resistor, a rheostat (variable resistor), an ammeter and a voltmeter.
questions.answer: Cell: one long thin line (+) and one short thick line (−). Battery: two or more cells joined. Closed plug key: a key symbol with a dot (plug) in it. Resistor: a zig-zag line. Rheostat: a zig-zag with an arrow across it. Ammeter: a circle with A. Voltmeter: a circle with V.

questions.q: A potential difference of 6 V is applied across a 24 Ω resistor. Find the current. What will the current be if the potential difference is doubled?
questions.answer: I = V/R = 6/24 = 0.25 A. If V is doubled to 12 V, I = 12/24 = 0.5 A: the current also doubles (Ohm's law).

questions.q: Wire P has length L and area of cross-section A. Wire Q, made of the same material, has length 2L and area of cross-section 4A. Compare their resistances.
questions.answer: R_{P} = ρL/A. R_{Q} = ρ(2L)/(4A) = ½ × ρL/A. So the resistance of Q is half that of P.

questions.q: A nichrome wire 2 m long, with an area of cross-section of 0.5 mm^{2}, has a resistance of 4 Ω. Find the resistivity of nichrome.

sections.title: Day 2: Resistors in series and parallel

questions.q: Resistors of 3 Ω, 6 Ω and 9 Ω are connected in series. The equivalent resistance is:
questions.answer: (c) 18 Ω: in series, R = 3 + 6 + 9

questions.q: Resistors of 6 Ω and 3 Ω are connected in parallel. The equivalent resistance is:
In a parallel combination of resistors, which quantity is the same for every resistor?
questions.answer: (b) the potential difference

questions.q: You have three 6 Ω resistors. How will you connect them to get an equivalent resistance of (a) 9 Ω, (b) 4 Ω?
questions.answer:
(a) Two in parallel (3 Ω), then that pair in series with the third: 3 + 6 = 9 Ω.
(b) Two in series (12 Ω), then that pair in parallel with the third: (12 × 6)/(12 + 6) = 4 Ω.

questions.q: Resistors of 5 Ω, 10 Ω and 15 Ω are connected in series to a 6 V battery. Find the current and the potential difference across each resistor.

Resistors of 10 Ω and 40 Ω are connected in parallel, and this combination is connected in series with a 2 Ω resistor and a 10 V battery. Find (i) the total resistance, (ii) the current from the battery, (iii) the current through the 10 Ω and 40 Ω resistors.
questions.answer:
(i) Parallel part: (10 × 40)/(10 + 40) = 8 Ω. Total = 8 + 2 = 10 Ω.
(ii) I = 10/10 = 1 A.
(iii) Potential difference across the parallel part = 1 × 8 = 8 V. Current through 10 Ω = 8/10 = 0.8 A; through 40 Ω = 8/40 = 0.2 A. (Check: 0.8 + 0.2 = 1 A.)

questions.q: Which has the higher resistance: a 100 W bulb or a 60 W bulb, both rated for 220 V? Show by calculation.
questions.answer: R = V^{2}/P. 100 W bulb: 220 × 220/100 = 484 Ω. 60 W bulb: 220 × 220/60 ≈ 807 Ω. The 60 W bulb has the higher resistance.

sections.title: Day 3: Heating effect and electric power

questions.q:
**Assertion (A):** Electric power is measured in kilowatt-hours.
**Reason (R):** 1 kWh = 3.6 × 10^{6} J.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.
questions.answer: (d) A is false: the kWh is a unit of energy; power is measured in watts. R is true.

questions.q: The heat produced in a resistor is H = I^{2}Rt. If the current is doubled, the heat produced in the same time becomes:
questions.answer: (d) four times, because heat depends on the square of the current

questions.q: In a circuit, a fuse is connected:
options: between the earth wire and the neutral wire
questions.answer: (a) in series with the device, so that it breaks the circuit when the current is too high

questions.q: An electric kettle is rated 880 W, 220 V.

subparts.q: Find the resistance of its heating element.
Fuses of 2 A, 5 A and 15 A are available. Which one should be used for the kettle? Why?
subparts.answer: The 5 A fuse. It is a little above the normal current of 4 A, so it will not blow in normal use but will melt if the current rises dangerously. A 2 A fuse would blow at once; a 15 A fuse would not protect the kettle.

questions.q:
(a) Starting from P = VI, show that P = I^{2}R and P = V^{2}/R.
(b) A motor draws a current of 3 A from a 220 V supply. Find its power, the energy it uses in 5 hours (in kWh), and the cost if electricity costs ₹6 per unit.
questions.answer:
(a) Using V = IR: P = VI = (IR)I = I^{2}R. Using I = V/R: P = V(V/R) = V^{2}/R.
(b) P = VI = 220 × 3 = 660 W = 0.66 kW. Energy = 0.66 × 5 = 3.3 kWh (3.3 units). Cost = 3.3 × 6 = ₹19.80.

questions.q: The 100 W and 60 W bulbs from Day 2 are connected in series to a 220 V supply. Which one glows brighter? Explain.
questions.answer: The 60 W bulb. In series, the same current flows through both, so the power used (P = I^{2}R) is greater in the bulb with the higher resistance. The 60 W bulb has the higher resistance (about 807 Ω against 484 Ω), so it glows brighter.

closing: Write the formula, substitute, then the unit. That's 3 marks every time!
